title: CINEMETA
tagline: A movie recommender built for the cold-start problem — personal from a user’s first session, with a reason for every pick.
overview: CINEMETA is a full-stack movie recommendation platform designed for users the system knows nothing about yet. A five-step onboarding captures seed films, genres, languages, moods and limits on rating and runtime. A two-stage engine — multi-channel candidate retrieval, then stage-aware ranking — turns that into recommendations, each with a confidence score and a plain-language reason. As the user likes, dislikes, rates and watchlists films, the engine shifts how much it trusts each signal.
problem: Recommenders that learn from ratings have nothing to work with when someone first arrives — the cold-start problem. Most apps fall back to “popular now”, which is generic exactly when a user is deciding whether the product understands them.
motivation: My final-year project in Information Science and Engineering at RVITM (Project Work, 2026–27). Cold start is a well-known open problem in recommender systems, and solving it well needs the onboarding flow, the data model and the ranking logic to be designed together.
objectives: Collect enough taste signal in onboarding to personalise the very first recommendations
Adapt the ranking as a user moves from cold start to an established profile
Explain every recommendation in plain language, with a confidence score
Use real movie metadata from TMDb, with a local fallback when the API is unavailable
Ship a complete product: accounts, watchlist, ratings, reviews and an analytics view
features: Five-step onboarding: pick up to 8 seed films, favourite genres, languages, moods, minimum rating and maximum runtime
Taste profile with positive and negative signals — liked and disliked films, genres, directors, cast, moods and languages
Three user stages — cold start, few-shot and warm — chosen from how much the user has told the system
Candidate retrieval from four channels: thematic content, explicit preferences, seed-film prototypes and a Bayesian quality prior (~150 candidates)
Ranking over seven normalised signals whose weights change with the user’s stage
Penalty for films similar to what the user disliked
Diversity re-ranking (Maximal Marginal Relevance, λ = 0.8) so the list isn’t ten versions of one film
Explanation sentence, top matched reasons and a confidence score on every recommendation
“More like this” similar-movie search, trailers and streaming providers via TMDb
Natural-language movie search and an AI assistant powered by Gemini
Watchlist, likes, dislikes, watched history, ratings and reviews
MongoDB via Mongoose when configured, in-memory store otherwise; Docker Compose for the full stack

architecture.label: Onboarding & UI

workflow.title: Onboard
workflow.detail: The user picks seed films, genres, languages and moods, and sets minimum rating and maximum runtime.

workflow.title: Build the taste profile
workflow.detail: Seed films and preferences become weighted genre, keyword, director, cast, mood and language signals, plus a negative profile from dislikes.

workflow.title: Choose the stage
workflow.detail: Fewer than 2 signals is cold start, 2–7 is few-shot, 8 or more is warm.

workflow.title: Retrieve candidates
workflow.detail: Four channels each nominate films; their union forms a pool of about 150.

workflow.title: Rank
workflow.detail: Each candidate is scored on seven normalised signals. At cold start, language and genre carry the most weight; as the profile grows, content similarity rises from 14% to 36% of the score.

workflow.title: Diversify & explain
workflow.detail: MMR re-ranking trades a little relevance for variety; each pick gets a confidence score and a sentence explaining why.

workflow.title: Learn from feedback
workflow.detail: Likes, dislikes, ratings, watched and watchlist actions update the profile for the next request.

decisions.title: Stage-adaptive weights
decisions.detail: A new user’s explicit choices are the most reliable signal, so they dominate early; content similarity to their films takes over as evidence accumulates.

decisions.title: Two-stage retrieve-then-rank
decisions.detail: Cheap multi-channel retrieval narrows the catalogue before the more expensive scoring, and ensures candidates come from several kinds of evidence.

decisions.title: Normalise before weighting
decisions.detail: Every signal is min-max normalised to [0, 1] so the stage weights mean what they say.

decisions.title: Negative signals count
decisions.detail: Dislikes build a separate profile that penalises similar films instead of being ignored.

decisions.title: Explanations from the scoring itself
decisions.detail: Reasons are collected while each signal is computed, so the explanation reflects what actually drove the score.

decisions.title: Run anywhere
decisions.detail: MongoDB is optional — without a connection string the app runs on an in-memory store, and TMDb failures fall back to cached data.

challenges.challenge: Almost no signal for a new user
challenges.solution: A short, structured onboarding gathers several kinds of preference at once, and the cold-start weights lean on exactly those inputs.

challenges.challenge: Lists that are all the same kind of film
challenges.solution: Maximal Marginal Relevance re-ranking penalises candidates too similar to ones already chosen.
TMDb responses are cached and the app falls back to local data when requests fail.
Each recommendation carries its top reasons and a calibrated confidence score rather than a raw number.

testing: Includes an evaluation module that computes Precision@K, Recall@K, MAP, NDCG, hit rate, diversity and coverage for a recommendation list.

Relevance in that module is currently judged by heuristic rules (language match plus similarity or genre overlap), not held-out user ratings — so its numbers describe internal consistency, not real-world accuracy, and none are quoted here.
limitations: Ranking is content- and preference-based. There is no trained collaborative-filtering or matrix-factorisation model yet; the “collaborative” endpoint reuses the hybrid engine.
Stage weights are hand-tuned rather than learned.
Evaluation uses a heuristic relevance proxy instead of an offline split of real ratings.
Has not been tested with real users at scale.
improvements: Train a matrix-factorisation model on a public ratings dataset (e.g. MovieLens) and blend it in for warm users
Learn the stage weights from data instead of setting them by hand
Evaluate on held-out ratings and report Precision@K and NDCG honestly
Automated tests for the feature extractor and ranker
Public deployment with a demo account
verification: Written from the public CINEMETA repository (backend/ml, server.ts, src/components). Weights, thresholds and features listed here are taken from the code.
resumeStack: React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, MongoDB, TMDb API
resumePoints: Full-stack movie recommender for cold-start users: a five-step onboarding builds a taste profile used for the very first recommendations.
Two-stage engine with four-channel retrieval, seven-signal ranking whose weights adapt to the user’s stage, MMR diversity re-ranking and a plain-language reason for every pick.
